newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU to cost Deutsche 400 mln DM - Breuer.
newsitem.headline: EMU to cost Deutsche 400 mln DM - Breuer.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG must spend 400 million marks to manage the switch to Europe's single currency, newly-appointed chief executive Rolf Breuer told Focus magazine in an interview released at the weekend.

Breuer told Focus that coping with the transition to the euro currency was "much more complicated than you would think" and would require the bank's computers to manage transactions in parallel in both euros and marks.

He said the bank had to be ready to offer service to its customers from January 1, 1999, when the euro is introduced as a book-keeping unit, if they want to do business in the new international currency.
"We can't tell out customers, 'sorry we aren't ready," Breuer said.

Breuer said European monetary union would shift the balance of Deutsche's business, with the bank's classical role as an intermediary between lenders and borrowers giving way more to investment banking.

Deutsche, Europe's largest bank, has pursued an aggressive strategy to expand its investment banking activities in recent years. Breuer said, however, he had no plans to make further acquisitions in North America at the moment.
In the longer term, Deutsche is looking to become one of top five global players in the banking business, he added.
Deutsche ranks third in money and bond operations, in the top ten in share dealings, but will need years to catch up in the investment banking business, Breuer told Focus.
